S A wiper trip was performed before proceeding with the logging program. The pipe was worked in the section where first stuck in the interval 15780-15875 ft MD. No tight hole was encountered. No fill was observed at the bottom of the hole. After the wiper trip, the RFT/GR was run in hole in order to acquire formation pressure data and to assist in the planning of the production test in this section. T

The 26 hole opening proceeded with few problems apart from occasional overpull on tripping out which necessitated jarring of the drillstring. A total of 85 joints (including the hanger) K55 133 lb/ft 20 casing were run, with the casing shoe being set at 3467 ft. The casing was cemented with 787 bbls of ppg

units. Few other drilling problems arose whilst completing the section to 8280 ft. The hole angle at this point was 28 degrees with an azimuth of 139 degrees. After circulating bottoms up an attempt was made to pull to the shoe. Overpull of 212 Klbs and swabbing of mud occurred on the first few stands pulled. At around 6600 ft the string became stuck and had to be jarred free. Once at the shoe the string was run back

ue to increasing circulating pressures and very high mud temperatures (up to 170 deg.F in the ditch). On many occasions only one pump was in operation as the other was repaired. At 12504 ft the hole began to pack off and 200 Klbs overpull was recorded as the pipe was worked. The situation was hindered because both rig pumps were undergoing maintenance.
